institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to go on exchange in an Arctic area, since it is very politically relevant nowadays.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Tromsø is a great place, no doubt about that. It is almost impossible not to consider to move there permanently, it is that amazing and unique.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, though one needs to do their research on the university's website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of help from my roomies who were local, and two of them were guides in the orientation week for internationals. So I guess anyone can ask the guides about anything during the orientation week, they are all students at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Upon arrival everything was fine, but it could be nice to receive more assistance before the arrival.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy, not at all. I was probably very lucky. I applied for housing at the end of March and that was barely enough, and my semester started on August.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The distance from the university doesn't matter that much because it is a small island. Of course there are places that are better than others, but in the end the public transport is ok, and in the worst case the walk won't be too long. Just make sure you apply for student housing VERY early. Many students did not get any student housing and had to look for housing on the private market, that is a lot more expansive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again - apply for student housing as early as you can!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It could be easier, as I mentioned, one should do their research. But very detailed instructions are given, you just need to do your research about the courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to submit an application through the student web, and you have instructions for it on the university's website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The instructions on the website are very detailed, but things like email or a phone call weren't available. Only when I got accepted, someone from the chemistry department helped me with the final choice of the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I of course checked everything with my "studievejleder" first, but the schedule of the courses wasn't available at first, only late in the process. So after I saw the schedule I changed some of the courses to avoid overlap. But that caused some delay in the disbursement of my Erasmus grant.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research about the courses as early as you can and maybe also try to receive the schedule somehow, so you can get an overview of how the courses overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses were better than others. In some of them I didn't feel that I have learned much, while others were very relevant and up-to-date. Also, it was easier to choose an elective that was out of my field, since everything was on the same campus.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say it is lower than in UCPH, at least in the courses I took.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, you have lectures and exercises just like in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Biological chemistry, General pharmacology and toxicology and my elective - Arctic Norway: aspects of politics, government and international relations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My elective, the Arctic Norway course. It is very relevant, especially when you are in the Arctic yourself. It really gives you the big picture of the geopolitics of the area. I was very interested in this topic, and it was also one of the reasons why I chose Tromsø, so I was glad I could learn much about it from this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The overall cost is expensive, so my advice - calculate how much money you need - and add more to it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol are expensive, the transport, however, is very cheap. The monthly ticket is less than 250 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: almost everyone I know were a part of a club. It can be anything - sports, sailing, choir, board games, etc. They will all present themselves during the orientation week and after.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again, there were so many, also depends on which club you are apart of, but there were also activities available for everyone, like "waffle Friday" and trips and tours, art workshops etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally like hiking and discovering new places, so I would definitely recommend the activities made by the organization ESN. They organize tours but also really nice workshops.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: What's wonderful about Tromsø area is that everything is beautiful around you. You just need to choose where to go and it will be worth it. My favorites were Sherpatrappa, Ersfjordbotn, Sommarøy and Lyngen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is not too different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Come to the orientation week! And try to be present in most organized activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The alcohol and party culture are a bit different, but I guess that also depends on your social circle. 
But I didn't find anything to be challenging, not the culture at least, just the climate...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I felt a lot of freedom while being there. It seems that you can just "do your own thing" and it is acceptable. People seem very liberal and open - also towards internationals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for housing as early as you can
2. Come to the orientation week
3. Save a lot of money

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will get all the information you need during the orientation week, but if you have local students in your courses or your housing, it can be very useful to ask them about anything - the studies, life in the city and other good tips.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature. Absolutely astonishing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To deal with the fact that it is over...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Going on exchange requires a lot of bureaucracy, but it is totally worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
